# Part A
Test the whitening function:

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Generate a multivariate time series-like dataset
n <- 1000
p <- 3

# Create correlated variables with different scales
A <- matrix(c(
  2.0,  0.8,  0.3,
  0.5,  1.5,  0.7,
  0.2, -0.4,  1.0
), nrow = p, byrow = TRUE)

E <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)
X <- E %*% t(A)

# Add a nonzero mean to each variable
X <- sweep(X, 2, c(5, -3, 10), "+")

# Check the original covariance
cat("Covariance before whitening:\n")
print(round(cov(X), 3))

# Apply the whitening function
Z <- whiten_data(X)

cat("\nCovariance after whitening:\n")
print(round(cov(Z), 6))

cat("\nMeans after whitening:\n")
print(round(colMeans(Z), 10))
```

Test the function that returns the autocovariance matrices for a set of lags:

```{r}
lags <- 1:5

# Use the same standardized test set as above
Sigma_lags <- autocov_matrices(Z, lags = lags)
Sigma_lags
```
# Part B

We test the fixed block and the stationary bootstrap. The implementation functions are in separate R-files.

We use the same data as before to demonstrate how the bootstrap methods preserve local dependence and to investigate how the choice of block length, or expected block length for the stationary bootstrap, affects the resampled series.

We start by inspecting how the bootstrap methods preserve local dependence compared to iid methods.

```{r}
# we use the setting 1 simulation data, because we know that it at has autocorrelation. 
set.seed(123)
X <- generate_ladle_data(n = 2000)
Z <- whiten_data(X)

n <- nrow(Z)
# iid bootstrap of Z
# one replicate
i_s <- sample(seq_len(n), size = n, replace = TRUE)
replicate_iid <- Z[i_s, , drop = FALSE]

block_bootstrap_replicate <- block_bootstrap(data = Z, B = 5)

stationary_bootstrap_replicate <- stationary_bootstrap(data = Z, B = 5)

max_lag <- 30

acf_original <- acf(Z[, 1], lag.max = max_lag, plot = FALSE)
acf_iid <- acf(replicate_iid[, 1],
                    lag.max = max_lag, plot = FALSE)
acf_mbb <- acf(block_bootstrap_replicate[, 1],
                    lag.max = max_lag, plot = FALSE)
acf_sb <- acf(stationary_bootstrap_replicate[, 1],
                    lag.max = max_lag, plot = FALSE)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(acf_original, main = "Original series")
plot(acf_iid, main = "IID bootstrap")
plot(acf_mbb, main = "Moving block bootstrap (B = 5)")
plot(acf_sb, main = "Stationary bootstrap (L = 5)")


```


Better check numerically than use many plots...

```{r}
# Extract sample autocorrelations at lags 1, ..., max_lag
get_acf <- function(x, max_lag = 20) {
  as.numeric(acf(x, lag.max = max_lag, plot = FALSE)$acf)[-1]
}

max_lag <- 20
n_boot <- 200

# Original ACF for component 1
acf_original <- get_acf(Z[, 1], max_lag)

# IID bootstrap replicates
set.seed(789)

acf_iid_reps <- replicate(n_boot, {
  idx <- sample(seq_len(n), size = n, replace = TRUE)
  get_acf(Z[idx, 1], max_lag)
})

# Summarize the average ACF and its deviation from the original
iid_mean_acf <- rowMeans(acf_iid_reps)
iid_mae <- mean(abs(iid_mean_acf - acf_original))
iid_mae

compare_bootstrap <- function(Z, block_lengths, method,
                              n_boot = 200, max_lag = 20) {
  original_acf <- get_acf(Z[, 1], max_lag)
  results <- lapply(block_lengths, function(L) {
    acf_reps <- replicate(n_boot, {
      if (method == "mbb") {
        Z_star <- block_bootstrap(data = Z, B = L)
      } else if (method == "sb") {
        Z_star <- stationary_bootstrap(data = Z, B = L)
      } else {
        stop("Unknown bootstrap method")
      }
      get_acf(Z_star[, 1], max_lag)
    })

    mean_acf <- rowMeans(acf_reps)

    data.frame(
      block_length = L,
      mean_abs_error = mean(abs(mean_acf - original_acf)),
      lag1_original = original_acf[1],
      lag1_bootstrap = mean_acf[1]
    )
  })
  do.call(rbind, results)
}

results_mbb <- compare_bootstrap(
  Z, block_lengths, method = "mbb",
  n_boot = 200, max_lag = 20
)

results_sb <- compare_bootstrap(
  Z, block_lengths, method = "sb",
  n_boot = 200, max_lag = 20
)

plot(results_mbb$block_length, results_mbb$mean_abs_error,
     type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Block length",
     ylab = "Mean absolute ACF error",
     main = "ACF preservation by block length")

lines(results_sb$block_length, results_sb$mean_abs_error,
      type = "b", pch = 17, lty = 2)

legend("topright",
       legend = c("Moving block", "Stationary"),
       pch = c(19, 17), lty = c(1, 2))
```


# Part C

Check the ladle functions for simulated data:

```{r}
set.seed(385)

# Change these to test both boot strap methods and diagonalizers
res <- diagonalizer_full(data = Z, 
                         lags = 1:12, 
                         n_boot = 200, 
                         bootstrap_method = stationary_bootstrap, 
                         block_size = 20, 
                         diagonalizer = SOBI_diagonalizer)

B_hat <- res$B_hat
B_star <- res$B_star # the array containing b_stars
lambda <- res$lambda

p <- length(lambda)

# Check phi function
lambda_values <- sort(as.numeric(lambda), decreasing = TRUE)
k_values <- 0:(p-1)

phi_values <- vapply(k_values, function(k) {
  phi(lambda, k)
}, numeric(1))

data.frame(
  k = k_values,
  eigenvalue_squared = lambda_values,
  phi = phi_values
)


# Check orthonormality of U_tau
# Original estimate
max(abs(crossprod(B_hat) - diag(ncol(B_hat))))

# One bootstrap estimate
B_star_1 <- B_star[, , 1]

max(abs(crossprod(B_star_1) - diag(ncol(B_star_1))))

p <- nrow(B_hat)

f0_values <- sapply(0:(p - 1), function(k) {
    f_0_k(B_hat, B_star, k)
  })


f_values <- sapply(0:(p - 1), function(k) {
  f_k(B_hat, B_star, k)
  })

data.frame(
  k = 0:(p - 1),
  f0 = f0_values,
  f = f_values
)

# Compute full criterion and estimate the dimension
g_values <- sapply(0:(p - 1), function(k) {
  g_k(lambda, B_hat, B_star, k)
})

results <- data.frame(
  k = 0:(p - 1),
  phi = phi_values,
  f = f_values,
  g = g_values
)
results

k_hat <- results$k[which.min(results$g)]
k_hat
```


# Part D Simulation Study 

Now we use the simulation setting specified as Setting 1 in the paper to investigate the behaviour of our implementation.

First we test the methods once and plot the results of f, phi and g to verify the results are as expected. We use the stationary bootstrap method, expected block size of 20 and the SOBI estimator here. 

```{r}
set.seed(469)

X <- generate_ladle_data(n = 2000)
Z <- whiten_data(X)
p <- ncol(Z)

# Setting 1 parameters
tau = 1:12
n_boot = 200
block_size = 20
bootstrap_method = stationary_bootstrap
diagonalizer = SOBI_diagonalizer


res <- diagonalizer_full(data = Z, 
                         lags = tau, 
                         n_boot = n_boot, 
                         bootstrap_method = bootstrap_method, 
                         block_size = block_size, 
                         diagonalizer = diagonalizer)

B_hat <- res$B_hat
B_star <- res$B_star
lambda <- res$lambda

k_values <- 0:(p-1)
f_s <- sapply(k_values, function(k){f_k(B_hat, B_star, k)})
phi_s <- sapply(k_values, function(k){phi(lambda, k)})
g_s <- f_s + phi_s

```

```{r}
plot(k_values, f_s,
     type = "b",
     xlab = "Component",
     ylab = "Criterion",
     col = "black",
     ylim = c(0, 0.5),
     xaxt = "n")

axis(1, at = k_values)

lines(k_values, phi_s, type = "b", col = "red")
lines(k_values, g_s, type = "b", col = "green")

legend("topright",
       legend = c("f", expression(phi), "g"),
       col = c("black", "red", "green"),
       pch = 1)
```

Next we repeat the bootstrapping and estimation to gauge the error.


```{r}
# with simulation
# this takes a minute to run
# with AMUSE
set.seed(20261024)

k_values <- 0:9
R <- 100
n_boot <- 200
true_q <- 5

signal_dim_estimates_AMUSE <- replicate(R, {
  X <- generate_ladle_data(n = 1500)
  Z <- whiten_data(X)

  res <- diagonalizer_full(
    data = Z,
    lags = 1,
    n_boot = n_boot,
    bootstrap_method = stationary_bootstrap,
    block_size = 10,
    diagonalizer = AMUSE_diagonalizer
  )

  g_s <- vapply(
    k_values,
    function(k) g_k(res$lambda, res$B_hat, res$B_star, k),
    numeric(1)
  )

  k_values[which.min(g_s)]
})

summary(signal_dim_estimates_AMUSE)

# Proportion selecting the correct dimension
mean(signal_dim_estimates_AMUSE == true_q)

# Monte Carlo standard error of the correct-selection rate
sqrt(
  mean(signal_dim_estimates_AMUSE == true_q) *
  (1 - mean(signal_dim_estimates_AMUSE == true_q)) / R
)

# Distribution of estimated dimensions
table(signal_dim_estimates_AMUSE)
```

This takes about 30 minutes:

```{r}
# same thing
# with SOBI
set.seed(20261024)

signal_dim_estimates_SOBI <- replicate(R, {
  X <- generate_ladle_data(n = 1500)
  Z <- whiten_data(X)

  res <- diagonalizer_full(data = Z, 
                         lags = 1:12, 
                         n_boot = n_boot, 
                         bootstrap_method = stationary_bootstrap, 
                         block_size = 10, 
                         diagonalizer = SOBI_diagonalizer)

  g_s <- vapply(
    k_values,
    function(k) g_k(res$lambda, res$B_hat, res$B_star, k),
    numeric(1)
  )
  k_values[which.min(g_s)]
})

summary(signal_dim_estimates_SOBI)

# Proportion selecting the correct dimension
mean(signal_dim_estimates_SOBI == true_q)

# Monte Carlo standard error of the correct-selection rate
sqrt(
  mean(signal_dim_estimates_SOBI == true_q) *
  (1 - mean(signal_dim_estimates_SOBI == true_q)) / R
)

# Distribution of estimated dimensions
table(signal_dim_estimates_SOBI)
```



# Part E
We apply the methods to the time-series data set provided for the assignment in Moodle. We use both the fixed-block and stationary bootstrap versions of the ladle estimator.
```{r}
ts_data <- read.delim("timeseries.dat.txt", sep = " ", header = FALSE)
ts_data_cs <- whiten_data(ts_data)
p <- ncol(ts_data_cs)
```

Choosing block length
```{r}
for (i in 1:10){
  acf(ts_data_cs[, i])
}
```
Many acf plots show small autocorrelation even at lags 10 and 15. Let's try with 10. 

We estimate the ladle estimator for both bootstrap methods using (expected) block
length of B = 10 and evaluating SOBI with τ = 1, . . . 10 lags. 

```{r}
set.seed(469)
res_stat <- diagonalizer_full(data = ts_data_cs, 
                         lags = 1:10, 
                         n_boot = 200, 
                         bootstrap_method = stationary_bootstrap, 
                         block_size = 10, 
                         diagonalizer = SOBI_diagonalizer)
res_block <- diagonalizer_full(data = ts_data_cs, 
                         lags = 1:10, 
                         n_boot = 200, 
                         bootstrap_method = block_bootstrap, 
                         block_size = 10, 
                         diagonalizer = SOBI_diagonalizer)

k_values <- 0:(p-1)
g_stat <- sapply(k_values, function(k){g_k(res_stat$lambda, 
                                           res_stat$B_hat,
                                           res_stat$B_star, k)})
g_stat_min <- k_values[which.min(g_stat)]
g_block <- sapply(k_values, function(k){g_k(res_block$lambda, 
                                           res_block$B_hat,
                                           res_block$B_star, k)})
g_block_min <- k_values[which.min(g_block)]

plot(k_values, g_stat,
     type = "b",
     xlab = "Component",
     ylab = "g(k)",
     col = "black",
     ylim = c(0, 0.3),
     xaxt = "n")

axis(1, at = k_values)

lines(k_values, g_block, type = "b", col = "red")

legend("topright",
       legend = c("Stationary bootstrap", "Block bootstrap"),
       col = c("black", "red"),
       pch = 1)
```

Block length sensitivity analysis???


```{r}
set.seed(1234)
stat_minimums <- numeric(6)
block_minimums <- numeric(6)

for (B in 5:10) {
  res_stat <- diagonalizer_full(data = ts_data_cs, 
                         lags = 1:B, 
                         n_boot = 200, 
                         bootstrap_method = stationary_bootstrap, 
                         block_size = B, 
                         diagonalizer = SOBI_diagonalizer)
res_block <- diagonalizer_full(data = ts_data_cs, 
                         lags = 1:B, 
                         n_boot = 200, 
                         bootstrap_method = block_bootstrap, 
                         block_size = B, 
                         diagonalizer = SOBI_diagonalizer)

k_values <- 0:(p-1)
g_stat <- sapply(k_values, function(k){g_k(res_stat$lambda, 
                                           res_stat$B_hat,
                                           res_stat$B_star, k)})
g_stat_min <- k_values[which.min(g_stat)]
stat_minimums[B-4] <- g_stat_min
g_block <- sapply(k_values, function(k){g_k(res_block$lambda, 
                                           res_block$B_hat,
                                           res_block$B_star, k)})
g_block_min <- k_values[which.min(g_block)]
block_minimums[B-4] <- g_block_min

}
stat_minimums
block_minimums
```
